utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, good afternoon. Perhaps before we proceed, the Defence would like to indicate the following: As regards the present witness, we have received, but only yesterday evening or yesterday afternoon, documents which, so it seems, were disclosed for the first time on this date by the Prosecution. The documents concern this witness and a criminal complaint made by several persons against this witness. The issue is quite important. We didn't have enough time to proceed with the inquiry and we have not been able to prepare ourselves adequately for the cross-examination. So we believe that we will have to be obliged to ask the re-appearance of this witness because simply we cannot make time that does not exist. We cannot invent the additional time that we would need, so this time will have to be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... disclosure of a document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Indeed the two documents really were discovered yesterday morning and they were disclosed at the first opportunity, in accordance with the Rules. As I think has been indicated before, we do continuous searches of the millions of records that we have and the obligation to disclose is ongoing from the beginning to the end and we always try to disclose as soon as the documents come to our attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The documents are what, in fact, came to my attention really were but two or three pages that were directly relevant to this witness and immediately disclosed were the entire documents. Although I would not want to say what the Defence case is, the entire documents may not themselves be relevant to the issues in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will see then when the documents are there. We do understand that the Prosecution fulfilled its obligation to disclose documents and that the Defence takes the position that the late disclosure would cause them to ask the recall of the witness, if necessary. Let's first see what -- whether these documents will be tendered and what these documents are and perhaps then see what type of decision would be appropriate to take. If there is nothing else at this moment -- yes, Mr. Ierace. I can't imagine that you are there and you are not taking this witness, that perhaps you would like to hear from the Chamber some of the issues we discussed yesterday or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I am simply here to seek to reserve a total of 15 minutes at the end of this evening's session to raise a matter with you. It is in relation to the maps of the sniping and shelling incidents, if that is convenient, perhaps I could return at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will do that at the end of the day and we will deal with other procedural matters, such as lists of witnesses, et cetera. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness, Mr. Hadzic, into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hadzic. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Please be seated. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, when we last spoke we were discussing the role of the Civil Defence and perhaps we could take it up from there. Did the Civil Defence have any role or any tasks in doing anything to protect or to prevent civilian persons from being shot, sniped or being injured by shelling?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said yesterday that the civil protection carried out the -- kept the roads clear in the central parts of Dobrinja in order to protect the civilian population from snipers. And in these central settlements whenever it was possible to put up some kind of protection, containers or bags filled with earth or wrecked cars, they would be put in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. place so that the civilian population could pass safely without getting hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, could I ask the -- that the witness be handed Exhibit D85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From that document, can you see it is an order issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could it be put on the ELMO? D85 was not foreseen by the Chamber that we should bring it, so, therefore...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Firstly, could you look at the second page of that order and tell us if you know the person who signed it, and if so, who that person is.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was undergoing medical treatment because I was wounded, but this was signed by the chief of the staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you see on the front page of the document or maybe -- just for the record, this document is dated the 20th of March, 1993, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you see the subject matter there. Could you tell us what the subject matter is, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was passed by the Chief of Staff based on the order which came from the 1st Corps command, so he sent it down to the units. And it was usual for this to be done in this way. The people who worked in the corps command are trained officers and they looked on things in an ideal way, like they learned that at school. And when they talked about the establishment of lines, the establishment of lines in Dobrinja is something that was outside of the normal military doctrines, because, by all elements, the configuration of the positions, the density of the buildings, it was impossible to carry out the establishment of this second line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So -- well, just to insure that there are no translation difficulties, could you just read the first line of the order, in your own language, of course.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Carry out additional fortification of positions in the second line by making facilities of full range with a light cover. In order to carry out the works on the second line, exclusively engaged units of civil protection and in order to carry out the trenches, to dig the trenches on the first line, exclusively engage the men from the battalion units."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This order, you told us, is an order passed on to the units in your brigade on the base of an order from the corps command, is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably, because it was passed down to all the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, does the first line immediately after the subject matter indicate the basis of this order? Could you read the first line immediately after the subject matter, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of line under number two?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. There is, towards the top of the page, a heading.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Based on the order of the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps, confidential number 12/64-2."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now does this sentence indicate that this order was a reproduction of the order from the 1st Corps command?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection. I have an objection based on our doctrine which calls for citing the entire sentence instead of just a part of it. It seems that my colleague stopped halfway through the sentence and the sentence would need to be quoted fully because it goes -- it runs to four lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you another question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. This document was tendered on the 4th of April and was not admitted yet because we are still waiting for a translation. So, I think the whole problem would not have been there if the Chamber would have been provided by the Defence with a translation. As far as I can see it has not been done. So I fully agree with you that if we are dependent on the quoting lines, and if we are not in a position that we can read the other part of the line, which, of course, would take away the problem, because we could have -- we could create our own image of the context. But why is there no translation, so that D85.1 could have been presented as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence would like to apologise, but as you can see, we have a lot of work and this is something that has slipped by and we will try to accomplish this as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the Prosecution who usually does not read B/C/S that well has some information about the content of the -- could we have -- for example, provisional translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have a provisional translation. I am a little bit nervous of handing to the Court provisional translations, but I will try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Advise translation as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would perhaps quote the full line, if that would be any better, and then perhaps during the first break, Defence and Prosecution, are the only ones who understand this document, could find a way of providing a final translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The first sentence of the document says: "Based on the 1st Corps's Chief of Staff's order, strictly confidential number 12/64-2, already performed works on reinforcement of positions and a situation assessment on possible agressor's opinions operations in order to perform works more rapid and complete, therefore, I order: One..." And it goes on to say what it orders. Does that part of the order indicate the source of the order?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And would that explain the reference to the second line position above? If you look on the document, immediately above the part that I just read there is a section, "Subject Arrangement of the Second Line Position." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You indicated that, for practical purposes, the brigade in Dobrinja did not have second line defensive positions, however, you can see under section of the order marked "1", if you could have a look at that. And I think you just read it, it indicates that the Civil Defence units would be employed to do some work.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was sent to all brigade commands in the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps. Some brigades, because of their positions were perhaps able to do what was ordered. But, I repeat, we, in Dobrinja, because of the specific characteristics in Dobrinja were not able to establish a second line. Whenever we tried to do anything that had to do with a second line, it would result in chaos because physically it was impossible to do this. The psychological condition of the population was such that had we started to do anything, the population would start to leave the area. So the only way we could defend the civilian population in Dobrinja was to use only the first line of defence. And if you wish, I could give you an example about the significant advance of Serbian forces. During the offensive on Igman, when half the civilian population was ready and packed in Dobrinja and prepared to leave, this was the condition, the state of the citizens in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. This order, as it is now transmitted by your brigade headquarters to the units in your brigade, involves the Civil Defence doing some work, does it not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Have a look at the task that the Civil Defence has been given in this order and if you could summarise for the Court what were these tasks that the Civil Defence was asked to do.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see in this order, the places of the trenches were specified exactly in the central parts of Dobrinja, which enabled communication between certain settlements, so that the civilian population could use these passages and be protected from sniper activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: One moment. May I just.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I take it from your answer that the task of the Civil Defence was in the reinforcement of trenches to protect the civilian population in Dobrinja from sniping; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say "trenches" because that is a military term. I would say passages, the digging of passages so that the civilian population could use them for passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, was the Civil Defence subordinated to the army, in the sense that they were under the command of the brigade in Dobrinja or was there some other arrangement that you had with them?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The civil protection had a separate command, which was part of the civilian structures which were active at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the course of the period from the summer of 1992 to the summer of 1994, can you describe to the Court the artillery and mortar tactics employed by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in respect to Dobrinja, as far as you observed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main task of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in Dobrinja was to protect the parts of Dobrinja, to shell that part of Dobrinja, then they would stop with the shelling, the intense shelling, and then they would use the armoured units and the infantry to come into the settlement, take the population and take them away. That was the tactic. The minute they failed to do this then they would direct artillery fire at the place where they wished to come into the settlement or shell the entire settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Up until what point in the conflict would the Sarajevo Romanija Corps units come into the settlement, take the population and take them away? About when in the conflict did that stop happening?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened in 1992, but they were not able to do that in 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter would like to correct one word from the previous answer of the witness. Instead of "protect" it should say "select."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So you said that the minute they failed to be able to come into Dobrinja to take the population, they would direct artillery fire where they wished to come into the settlement or shell the entire settlement. When you say "shell entire settlement" could you briefly tell us what you mean? In particular, was the shelling confined to areas where you had your military units or was it spread right through the entire area of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I have to object regarding the manner of the question. Are we asking this witness about the specific line or the entire area of Dobrinja? I think that the issue is less drastic than the way it has been described by the Prosecution. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I then just rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say that they would shell the entire settlement, from your observation, did they shell any particular targets or was the shelling indiscriminate in the settlement?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were targeting the entire settlement at random.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to the use of the word "indiscriminate." We all know what it means. Because there is always a possibility of there being a target somewhere and, therefore, the question should be phrased in a more specific manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this could have perfectly been an issue you would raise during cross-examination. But would you please be selective in interrupting Mr. Stamp's examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you have spoken quite a few times about sniping. Could you describe to us what the sniping was like for the population of Dobrinja during 1993 up to the summer of 1994.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war, including 1993 and 1994 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Excuse me. For the sake of time, I am going to ask you to confine your answer. Tell us about the period between the summer of 1992 to the summer of 1994, and not throughout the war. Just, please, if you could tell us what the sniping was like on the civilians in Dobrinja between the summer of 1992 to the summer of 1994.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Briefly, it was horrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only did the French booth say several times "1993," instead of 1992. I think we are talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the French translation, it could create no confusion. You are the only one listening to the French channel, and we do it at the end of the hearing. So may I again ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, of course 1993 was mentioned at least once, but let's not spend time on it. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, again, interruptions and objections when there is a good reason to do so. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question was: Can you describe for the Court the sniping tactics employed by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps during the period August or September 1992 to August 1994.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all elevated points, whenever it was possible to put sniping nests, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps did it, in order to shoot at the population. Also, when it comes to these communication passages, whenever someone strayed away from that passage or from those communication trenches they would become targets and consequently victims of sniping. Snipers even shot at the members of the international forces who came to deliver us food. Quite a few of them were wounded or killed. They didn't choose their targets. Everyone could become a target. An elderly person, a child, a dog or a cat, everything that moved would be targeted and shot at.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in respect to persons who were injured, the casualties from the sniping and the shelling, did -- was a medical facility created in Dobrinja to accommodate these person?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an area that we used as a hospital. It was a make-shift hospital where we could admit these people, the wounded people. The less severe cases were dealt with by us, but the most serious cases, after the initial treatment at our hospital, would be sent then to one of the Sarajevo hospitals.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who was the head of that makeshift hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Hadzir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is Dr. Jusuf Hadzir. Now, in relation to where the brigade headquarters was, how far away was this make-shift hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hospital was located almost at the very centre of Dobrinja, some hundred or -- between 50 and 100 metres away from the headquarters. Because in that building, before the war, there used to be a small department of a children's clinic, an out-patient children's clinic, and this is where we organised this make-shift hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, was the area in which your headquarters was shelled?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was shelled as much as any other neighbourhood, any other part of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How about the hospital? Can you say if there was any shelling in respect to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as intensely --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. I object to this question because there is a claim here that the hospital was exposed under shelling. So, instead of asking the question, whether there was any shelling of the hospital, and furthermore, the distance, according to the witness, between the headquarters and the hospital was 50 metres. So in view of that and a number of other things that we already know about, this question is rather leading and contentious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Much of what we know, is probably going to be the subject of argument at the appropriate time. Having regard to the evidence that has gone on before, I would submit that the question is not a leading question, however, I could rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. So the question was whether you can say there was any shelling in respect of the -- in respect to the hospital and you commenced answering: "Not as intensely." And then what would be the rest of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every single part of Dobrinja was exposed to severe shelling. One couldn't single out a specific area and say that it was shelled the more intensely than other parts. Thousands of shells were landing at the time. It was raining shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you, having been the commander of the brigade, can you tell us, if you can, what was the main sniper nest or sniper places from which there was sniper fire into Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period of time do you want me to talk about?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From September 1992 to August 1994, what were the primary areas in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps territory that sniping fire was directed into Dobrinja from?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most intense sniping came from the tower of the Orthodox church and also from high-rise ground in Dobrinja IV. The Airport Settlement and the village which was controlled by the Serb forces, looking towards the area of Dobrinja. Looking towards Mojmilo and Alipasino Polje, it was the Catholic university, the children's community centre, Sanjak House and all other major elevated points where snipers could be placed. But those were the most prominent points.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said the Catholic university. Is that institution known by any other name or designation?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it dominates the area of Nedzarici near the river because of its height, and it covers the area between the junction in Nedzarici, all the way up to Dobrinja V. Perhaps even as far as the village. I know it as a Catholic university or a university of theology. Sniper nests were always there, as well as other weapons which were covering the approach roads to Dobrinja where about 137 people were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to react, because I think it is very important. The French booth did not seize two lines on page 15. I am referring to lines 18 and 19. They have been only partially translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, at the end of the session, any comments on the French translation. No one, apart from you, is listening to the French channel, as far as I am aware of. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp. I did say this 15 minutes before to you as well. I would like you to listen to what I say. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am obliged, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Sanjak House, hopefully I have the pronunciation correct, where was that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have the pronunciation correct. It was located on a hill on a slope between the home for mentally retarded children and the old people's home which actually that never started working. It dominated the whole area, the whole hill and it covered the area between the junction in Nedzarici all the way to Alipasino Polje and Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You mentioned the Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that was one of the -- that was one of the areas of the most intense sniping came from. Can you say when that church was built? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. The work started before the war. I don't think it was ever fully completed, but the tower was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said the tower was there, that is, during the war?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Would you be able to identify that area or that position, if I showed you a photograph of the area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I respectfully ask if I could show the witness a photograph which was used in the opening of this case. The photograph at that time did have on it certain markings, however, I think those markings, having regard to the earlier ruling or the ruling this Court made in regard to another issue, that those writings be covered, and that is all that is covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is covered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember what the MFI number is, just for the record Mr. Stamp? If you could find out and then inform us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you hold it into the position so that Court in particular and the Defence as well could.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has pointed to a spot that I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now no one can see. Could perhaps the part the witness is pointing to be put a bit lower on the ELMO? Would that be of any assistance? Mr. Usher, would you please put it down so that we -- yes, there we are. And could you please point at it again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is pointing to an elevated structure towards the top of the photograph and to the left of the photograph. I am trying to find a unique --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be approximately one-third from the left of the photograph, a bit less perhaps, structured right under the top of the photograph, consisting of a building with one tower which seems to be rather wide, apart from the very very top of that tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I could describe it: A building with a dome in the middle and a higher tower to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, would you please ask the witness, those buildings which are below the church, belong to which settlement, which neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, could you just point to that line of building below the church.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us what was the name of this community and which part of Dobrinja was that at?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part of Dobrinja is Dobrinja IV, which was captured by the Serb forces as early as in April or May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please keep it a bit closer to us so we can see the whole picture. Please continue, Mr. Stamp, and we will listen carefully at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to shelling of Dobrinja, can you tell us the main locations from which the shells were fired into Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our intelligence information that was gathered by the people who were in charge of that, these were the locations of the, for instance, Nedzarici Barracks. The area below the University of Theology in Nedzarici, the area near Kasindolska Street. Mortar positions or batteries in Krtelji, Gornji Kotarac, Gavrica Brdo, the Lukavica Barracks, and the playground right above the barracks, there. There were quite a few of such locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now where would this intelligence information come from, can you indicate that to us?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our people probably managed to gather such information from those individuals who were located at the various observation points and the people who, during the war, had fled from their side over to the other side and brought with them relevant information. They probably had other intelligence sources that I couldn't tell you, that I am not able to tell you about. But they managed to gather this type of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you tell us, general, as brigade commander, were you aware of what type of mortars they had in Nedzarici, in the Nedzarici area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two types of shells in the area of Nedzarici, 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you say from your -- well, having lived in Dobrinja, when they were shelling at Dobrinja, would you be able to tell sometimes where it was being shelled from?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Nedzarici, one could hear the actual firing of mortar shells quite clearly. Dobrinja is a rather acoustic area and one could hear the firing there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like to take you to a couple particular days during the conflict. Can you recall the 1st of June, 1993? Did something significant happen on that day?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I will never forget that day. Two shells hit Dobrinja and killed 15 children. 21 -- 121 people were wounded, 56 out of them, severely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately what was the proportion of civilians to military persons among the casualties in that incident of that day?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you the exact number, but I think it was 50-50, roughly speaking. But that's not very important. Children died. Children who wanted to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Among --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, could the witness be shown D25 and D25.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes please, Mr. Usher, could you assist. Mr. Stamp, if you intend to rely on more exhibits that were admitted earlier, I think Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it is handy to give a list already to the Registrar so she can prepare already finding the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that a report which you sent to your corps command on the day of this incident?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the report of the officer on duty to the command and these reports were sent regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, among your soldiers who were killed and injured in that event, were any of them engaged in any military activity at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were free.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What were they doing, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what people did when they left the lines, when they were off-duty. Obviously, some of them had gone out to play ball.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were there any significant military activity by any units in your brigade on that day?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think that was an exceptionally calm day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like to take you now --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher, you can take away that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I take you now to the 12th of February, 1993. Do you recall a significant event of that day? I beg your pardon. I withdraw that question. The 12th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was another sad day for Dobrinja. 15 civilians were killed at a gas station at the station on the C5 Dobrinja settlement and a number of civilians were wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us again was the place where these people were killed on that day, the 12th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the interpreters didn't catch the number of casualties. Could you please -- oh, the number of -- the number of wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say how many civilians were wounded on the 12th of July in the incident that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think, but I am not sure, this is the Serbian booth, I think it is a pump, and I think it was interpreted differently. So in order to avoid confusion, I would like to just state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think I heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is translated in English as "gas station."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely why I asked him the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us again, what place the people were at who were killed on the 12th of July 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat on that day, at the water pump in the line. So this was a hand pump which was located there. So about 14 people were killed there and 20 were wounded, people who came there to get their water supply, because the water was the main problem in our life in Dobrinja, and the Serb forces knew that very well because they shut down the main water supply to the settlement. So, we did the best we can to get water. We even drank industrial water from the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was that water pump, a water pump which was used by units of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade did not get supplies from that water pump, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you -- would you be in a position to mark on a map where that water pump was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I respectfully ask that he be allowed to mark the map which he had pre-marked in red and if he could do so with blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that a blue pen?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I am sorry, suppose he were to put the map -- it is upside down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to ask. Can you turn the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just put your initials right under that blue spot.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you put that on the ELMO so I can see what is happening, please. So we can all see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how far was that spot or is that spot that you just marked from the house which lead to the trench, which lead to the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is from 30 to 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, when did the tunnel -- you told us yesterday, I believe, that the tunnel came into operation on the 30th of July.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 30th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, prior to the 12th of July 1993 did that area attract mortar fire and if so, could you tell us if there was any particular pattern to the mortar fire in that area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no usual pattern. Just like the rest of Dobrinja, that part was shelled as well. There was no routine standard in the shelling, but just like all the other settlements, it was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the time of this incident, according to your evidence, the tunnel was not in use?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was still being dug.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you have military personnel posted in the vicinity of the tunnel around the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that place, no. But in the initial stage, that building was not used as the entrance to the tunnel. It is a little bit deeper inside the settlement. That is where the tunnel went down into the ground. But as the tunnel began to be used later, a checkpoint was made so that there was an entrance to the tunnel from the building which was near the pump where this incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what I am asking though, is on the 12th of July, did you have any military units or personnel posted in the vicinity of the entrance to your tunnel, to the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As commander of the Dobrinja Brigade, did you form a view as to whether the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was aware of where the tunnel entrance on your side, that is, on the Dobrinja side, was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that they knew the exact location of the entrance to the tunnel on our side. Had they known, perhaps it would have been hellish on that side, because at some points there were hundreds of soldiers and civilians who were waiting to get into the tunnel. The second part of the tunnel, they knew about and it was under fierce shelling, the entrance -- the exit from the tunnel was in Donji Kotorac was under intense fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just to be precise, you said at some points, "there were hundreds of civilians and soldiers who were waiting to get into the tunnel." That would be after the tunnel opened, would it not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the tunnel was opened and after the entrance was moved to this building, which the entrance to which is marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, on the 12th of July, where was the entrance?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in this circle on the map, which is indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, was the trench from the entrance to the building yet dug?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trench didn't go towards the building. There was no trench up to the road. The road was dug and the trench went from the road up to this house from where the tunnel, digging for the tunnel was started.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we just go over that a little bit. Or maybe I should just ask you to describe to the Court, what was located in that area on the 12th of July, not after the 12th of July when the tunnel opened, but on the 12th of July, 1993, what was located in that area that you have just pointed to and spoken about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From here you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From here there was a private house here and from there the tunnel -- the digging for the tunnel was started towards the other side. So it was gradually being inclined from the surface part and it was gradually dug to a depth of four metres. So the digging continued all the way to the other side. It's interesting to point out that the tunnel zone or the tunnel trench reached the water streams, but it was important to say that the water didn't flood the tunnel. We still managed to dig it through.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say the "water streams" you mean the streams beneath the airport?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, coming back towards what you said, and this is just for the record, you said from here there was a private house, and from there the tunnel, the digging for the tunnel was started towards the other side. I should indicate that the witness pointed to the circle on the red line that he had drawn before. Now, before the tunnel opened and on the 12th of July, that is the date I want you to focus on, on the 12th of July before the tunnel was opened for activity, what existed between where this little circle on the line is and the building to the north is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meadow, a clearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you turn your attention now, please to the 22nd of February, 1994. May I withdraw that question. The 22nd of January, 1994, do you recall an incident in which some children were killed in Alipasino Polje on that day?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of January in 1994. As far as I remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is it the 21st of January or the 22nd of January, or are you quite sure of the date?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I know that it was winter and that the children were killed while they were sledding. In the central part of Alipasino Polje in a part below the playground, a shell hit and killed the children while they were sledding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now between the area where the children were killed and Nedzarici, which was at that time occupied by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, did your brigade have any mortar batch positions?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you have 82-millimetre mortars at that time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Because that was not our area of responsibility. Alipasino Polje was not in the area of the responsibility of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How far north was -- or may I put it this way: Where did your area of responsibility stop going north?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communication which went from Nedzarici to Dobrinja, that was the border of our area of responsibility, including the Olympic village, Mojmilo, which was part of our area, part of our area of responsibility. So from Nedzarici towards Dobrinja, the right side of the settlement, Vojnicko Polje up until the cross-roads of the Olympic village Mojmilo, and then this part of Dobrinja, just as you entered Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said it was quite easy for one to clearly hear when shells were fired Nedzarici into Dobrinja. Can you or can you not comment upon whether or not that would obtain, if one was in Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object because this is a hypothetical question, it doesn't contain concrete, specific elements but just pure hypothesis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will try to be a little bit more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If one were in the area of Alipasino Polje where the children were killed, could one hear when shells were fired from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has already replied, but once again, this is a hypothetical question, assume and so on. Can we know -- and so on. But the witness wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know there, whether the witness was there and has been there at that time, but apart from that, sometimes questions can relate to human experience, and if you know distances, the sometimes you can tell something about what these distances mean in view of sight and of what you could hear, especially under the acoustic circumstances on which the witness testified before. So, the objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you now turn to the 4th of February, 1994. There was an incident of significance in Dobrinja. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please remind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there an incident in Dobrinja on the 4th of February, 1994 where persons were killed and injured in circumstances where humanitarian aid was being distributed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the time of that incident, were there any troop movements or military activity by your troops that day?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say what was the closest military installation you had? But before I ask that question, may I just ask this one: Do you know where the incident occurred on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say what was your closest military unit or activity or facility to where the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the front lines of defence towards the Kula or towards the warehouses of the Sedrenik Construction Company. So that is where our units were located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the witness is pointing at some place at the map at this very moment. Could you please repeat that, Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you are -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you say what you are pointing to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am pointing to the place where our units were, at the point that they were -- at the closest point to the location of the incident. And this is where the incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, since you have pointed to the place where the incident occurred and where your closest units were, could you put a small "tick" where the incident occurred and then "X" where your closest military units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness for the record writes a cross to the point where he pointed to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Put a "tick," if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the witness puts a "tick" looking like an "L" at the spot where he indicated the incident occurred. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- did you observe --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am being told, Mr. President, Your Honours that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is already 15 minutes to 4.00. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the interpreters and the technicians be willing to continue for five minutes so we can finish the examination-in-chief? I see nodding in the affirmative. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You have spoken about the sniping of civilians and the random shelling in Dobrinja, and that there were casualties among the civilians. How, in that period of time, did the civilians cope? Specifically, did you observe whether or not this shooting and shelling of civilians impacted on them psychologically?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed, yes. I think this had a deadening psychological effect on people. You never knew if you went out that whether something would happen to you or not. Especially if you tried to pretend that times were normal and if you tried to behave in a normal way, in that case, it is possible that you could become the victim of a sniper. The psychological state of the -- the psychological condition of the population was very very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already talked about -- not only because of the sniper activity, but because of the supply with water and the worry about their families, the lack of fuel. During that period, there was no electricity, no water, no wood, no gas. There was no telephone service. There was a general hopelessness and nobody could see an end to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have to ask you a follow-up question based on something you just said. Could you just tell me quickly, when you said that there was no telephone service, was this situation continuous through the period or did you have telephone service sometimes through the period September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the situation regarding the telephones, regarding the military telephone lines improved in 1994 because we laid down cables to Mojmilo. But the civilian population didn't have any telephone service.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is the examination-in-chief, may it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours. I beg your pardon. That is the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. We will adjourn until 20 minutes past 4.00 and then you will be cross-examined by the Defence, Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is it you that is going to cross-examine the witness? Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will take the witness for one part of the cross-examination and my colleague will take him in the second part of the cross-examination. But we will remain within the timeframe used by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzic, good afternoon. Can you confirm for us, Mr. Hadzic, that on the 24th and 25th of October, 2001, you gave a statement to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attach a map to this statement, the map that we discussed today?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday, Mr. Hadzic, at the beginning of the examination conducted by my learned colleague, and I am referring to the period 1992, 1993, and 1994, that prior to the outbreak of the conflict, you had worked in the Energoinvest company?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever actively involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which one, please?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you -- did you become a member of this party from the beginning -- at the beginning of its existence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When exactly did you join the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the year, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1991, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you became a member of the SDA, were you aware of the programme of this party?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "not entirely," what exactly do you mean? What part of the programme was familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was familiar with the part of the programme that advocated the equality of the peoples in the area of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, if I tell you that the programme of the SDA was the creation of an Islamic society and the establishment of Islamic authority based on the principles of Islamic declaration, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, did you ever attend the rallies organised by the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Hadzic, if I say that the rallies of the SDA were conducted with the usage of lot of symbols, national symbols?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at least, not the ones that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What rallies specifically did you attend? Were any such rallies organised in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hold any office, any function, in the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The Party for Democratic Action, did it, at any one point in time, establish its own army which was called the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you anything about that, because I was not a member of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of its existence?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the role of the Patriotic League, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you anything specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, in Dobrinja, were there any members of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Hadzic, that members of the Patriotic League on the 4th of May 1992, tried to organise or establish the Territorial Defence at Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many members participated in the founding of the Territorial Defence, how many members of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that, because I did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, were you aware of the fact that the Patriotic League had about 60 to 70.000 armed members in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. And besides, the figure is ridiculous. It is simply not logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the Patriotic League in the area of Dobrinja, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Poorly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "poorly," can you tell us how they were armed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were armed with make-shift rifles, hunting rifles, pistols, M-56 automatic rifles, old German automatic rifles. That kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of Dobrinja - I am referring to April and May 1992 - were there any other voluntarily, so to speak groups which were armed and which had joined the Territorial Defence there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several groups, but not all of them joined the Territorial Defence. And their members were very poorly armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there were several groups, can you tell us if these groups had any names?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an exact answer in that sense, but most of these groups were formed in specific neighbourhoods of Dobrinja, and then they would be called after that neighbourhood. For example, Dobrinja I, IV, V, II, C-5 and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Delta, Mamba, Topa's fighters, Tabija; were these the names of such groups?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Dobrinja, as far as I can recall. These names belonged or designated the groups that were organised in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, would you agree with me if I tell you that after the multiparty elections which were handled in Bosnia-Herzegovina, inter-ethnic tensions increased, was that the result of the multiparty elections?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really agree with you. At least when it comes to the company I worked for, such tensions could not be felt.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about your neighbourhood, Dobrinja, the part of town where you lived?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such tensions were not felt there either. People lived a normal life.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, yesterday you spoke about the presence of the Yugoslav People's Army in the month of May 1992, in the area of Dobrinja. Speaking of the Mojmilo hill, specifically, when did you personally see members of the JNA for the first time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 17th of March, 1992 that the units of the JNA came out to the Mojmilo hill, and took up positions at the water tower there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the unit in question was, the unit that captured the Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that it was the unit commanded by Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic, who at the time held the rank of major, would you agree with me, with this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit commanded by him, no, General Hadzihasanovic did not command this unit. The unit which was under his command was a larger unit located in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But those were units under his command?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that during that period of time, the leading positions within the JNA in the area of the 5th military district were occupied by persons such as Mr. Rasim Delic, Vehbija Karic and others?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I was not a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but yesterday you told us it was a Serb army. I should like to know what was the base for that assertion, if you were not familiar with the military issues?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that it was the units of the JNA that had taken up positions at the Mojmilo hill as far as I remember. Shortly after that, Albanian members of these units fled from the Mojmilo hill and the composition of the unit there changed. Serb soldiers arrived. They changed the flag and generally speaking, the composition of the unit there was changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you were familiar with the situation at the time in the area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to see it with my own eyes. My apartment overlooks the Mojmilo hill. I could plainly see what flag was hoisted there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, yesterday you also told us about the barricades that were set up in Dobrinja. When did this take place?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 4th of May, the barricade at Dobrinja was set up on the 4th of May and on the Dobrinja Mojmilo location, that is, it was set on the Dobrinja Mojmilo location which resulted in a complete encirclement of the Dobrinja neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us the fact that Dobrinja belonged to the Novi Grad municipality?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a Public Security Station in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned the 4th of May. Do you know that on that day, nine members of the JNA were brought to this police station who were subsequently tortured and killed.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read about this in the papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was that one of the reasons for the setting up of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. May I add something please? I think that these soldiers, at least, according to what I was able to read in the papers, were brought to the police station in Novi Grad on the 17th or the 18th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, on the 17th or 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that tortured and killed these people?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were cut off from the 4th of April [as interpreted]. Nobody could leave Dobrinja, nor could anyone enter Dobrinja during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, when was the Territorial Defence unit in Dobrinja established?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned the 5th of May, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just ask whether there is any confusion, Ms. Pilipovic. Until now, the blockade, as it was called, was said to have happened on the 4th of May. And we find now the 4th of April on page 39, line 20. Where it says "we were cut off from the 4th of April." Is this a mistake or are we talking about something different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a mistake, Your Honour. We were cut off on the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you testified yesterday about the departure of the residents of Dobrinja and the fact that at one point in time they left their homes there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure but I believe that they were members of various ethnic groups, however, the majority were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did the Serbs leave Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, in April.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many Serbs left Dobrinja, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly how many, but it was a large number, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me if I tell you that the departure of Serbs from Dobrinja was the consequence of physical and psychological abuse of various voluntary groups in Dobrinja which were organised along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the members of such groups went from apartment to apartment and marked Serb apartments in the area with the remark, with the warning that the -- to the effect that the Serbs should leave Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In April and May in the area of Dobrinja, do you know that there were several prisons in the area of Dobrinja where people were detained and tortured?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us the fact that in Dobrinja, while you lived there in 1992, 1993, and 1994, there were two restaurants by the name of Sunce and Baltazar?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was a cafe called Baltazar before the war. I don't know what became of it during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that this cafe, the Baltazar cafe was used as a prison for Serbs during the war, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, during the examination-in-chief, you spoke about the establishment of the 5th Motorised Brigade and told us that it was established on the 6th of July --

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the 5th, but the 1st Dobrinja Brigade. It was established on the 6th of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What specific units were active in the area of Dobrinja prior to the 6th of July? I am referring to military units.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I told you that there had been groups, voluntary groups of patriots who had organised themselves with the purpose of defending the area from incursions .

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like the witness to be shown a document -- a document at this point, which would then be marked --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have provided this document to my learned colleagues from the Prosecution and the interpretation booths.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, indeed we get some -- very well. We did get some documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, can you see in front of you a document signed by the assistant commander for morale, Hamdija Alagumdjia [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the left corner of this document, do we read "the 5th Motorised Brigade command"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, from this document, can we see that the Dobrinja and Airport Settlement Territorial Defence units were formed on the 6th of May?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd of May 1992, was the 1st Dobrinja Battalion formed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I am aware of the fact that it was established at one point in time, however, I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: According to this document, would the 6th of July, 1992 mark the day when the 1st Dobrinja Brigade was formed, the one which was later called the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you lived in the area in question during the relevant times. Can you tell us where the location of the Territorial Defence Staff for Dobrinja and Airport Settlement was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff was located in the same building where the hospital was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "hospital" are you referring to the children's clinic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the 1st Dobrinja Battalion headquarters was in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in the same building where the premises of the Jugodrvo company were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say in the same building where Jugodrvo was located what location do you have in mind? What street do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what street it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of facility was it? What kind of a building was it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an eight-storey building with several entrances.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this was the building where the headquarters of the 1st Dobrinja Battalion was located and that the residents of Dobrinja lived on the upper floors of this building?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us the members of the TO and the 1st Dobrinja Battalion, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have uniforms, weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had civilian clothes, and the weapons that I already mentioned. I explained how the people were armed, very poorly. They wore sneakers, jeans, whatever they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the Dobrinja Battalion, when it was formed, what was its area of responsibility in Dobrinja, in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dobrinja village and the Airport Settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your role in the Territorial Defence and in the Dobrinja Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any role.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly not. In a way, yes, but I wasn't actually a member of the Dobrinja Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you were not a member of the Dobrinja TO, does that mean that you were a member of some other TO?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this group of patriots and sportsmen, the people who got together in order to defend ourselves, we were covered by the IDs of the Republican Military Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that you were a member of the group which was operating as part of the republican police?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether this group that you belonged to, can you tell us where this group was located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance, on the premises of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the local commune" can you be more specific? Which local commune in Dobrinja you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobrinja IIA.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You, as a member of the police, can you tell us which weapons you had as a police military unit?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like the others in Dobrinja, very poorly. We had handguns, hunting rifles, perhaps we had one or two automatic rifles that people bought with their own money.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say you were at the republican police level. Can you tell us who was heading the police forces in Sarajevo at that time? The republican police.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
