utterances.text: When you say: "Kerim Loncarevic," are you saying that he was the commander of the police for the whole of Sarajevo or was he at the republican level?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the police, that you were a member of, as the member of the Dobrinja group, can you tell us whether it was under the command of Kerim Loncarevic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Kerim Loncarevic wrote a book?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the conflict in Sarajevo, can you tell us where was the Military Police active in the region of Dobrinja in 1992, 1993, and 1994, and where its command post was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The Military Police.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say 90, are you thinking of 1992 and do you also mean 1993 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The formation of the Dobrinja Brigade included a company of the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So are you saying that this Military Police company that you belonged to was part of the 5th or the Dobrinja Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all. Some people stayed -- some people didn't wish to join the Dobrinja Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that not all people wanted to join the Dobrinja Brigade, does that mean that the Military Police in Dobrinja divided?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say it divided. People simply left to join the units that they were already in. They didn't wish to be members of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to show a document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please assist, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D159. D159.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, do you have before you a document from the 8th of October, 1992, which was signed by Naim Beslagic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if states here "officer on duty, Beslagic, Naim" can you tell us which brigade he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Dobrinja Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, the document that is before you, item two, paragraph two states: "The formation of the 5th Mountain Brigade, it has been completed except for the Military Police Platoon which does not want to be placed under the command of this brigade. We will report to you about this matter separately." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the platoon of the military police which did not wish to join the 5th Motorised Brigade, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you are asking the wrong question. This is the transformation of the brigade from the 1st Dobrinja to the 5th Motorised Brigade and we really did have problems with people who had to accept the military structure. But some of the people that we had problems with remained in the Military Police of the 5th Dobrinja Brigade when we explained to them what the duties were, what they needed to do, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is the reason why the platoon and later the battalion of the Military Police did not become part of the 5th Dobrinja Brigade, the fact that they wanted to operate independently?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the 1st Dobrinja Brigade was formed on the 6th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the Military Police headquarters in Dobrinja was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until -- which date do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: After the 6th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a platoon, it is a company, and it was located across the street from the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, when you said that you had -- you knew that Mr. Loncarevic wrote a book, did you have any information about the operation "Kisik," "oxygen?"

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When I tell you that Mr. Kerim Loncarevic commanded this operation and the operation entailed the bringing in of explosives in oxygen bottles into a part of Sarajevo which was under the control of the TO and later the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would you accept this fact as true?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot accept something or not accept it, if I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you read Mr. Loncarevic's book?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally cooperate with Mr. Kerim Loncarevic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little, up until the 6th of July, very little. From the 6th of July, when I became the commander of the brigade, I had more problems with him than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you had problems with him, can you tell us what kind of problems you had with him?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That part of the Military Police which did not want to join the battalion was located in a building in Dobrinja and they created problems for us. There were fights, physical fights almost between them and our men. So that we made several attempts to move them further away from the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that they were physically separated from you, that they were in another building, can you tell us where that part of the Military Police was located that was under the command of Mr. Kerim Loncarevic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the location which was -- which used to be the Turbo, discotheque.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where that is in Dobrinja and which street?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the street, but it was in Dobrinja II-A.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, can you tell us if the members of that group, of Military Police, under the command of Kerim Loncarevic, which positions did they hold in that part of the city?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean what positions?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have -- did they hold certain positions?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how they were dressed? And I am thinking about uniforms and also what kind of weapons they had.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were armed the same as the other people in Dobrinja were armed, and they also had civilian clothes. With the establishment of the 1st Dobrinja Brigade, we established the area of responsibility of the battalion and we did not permit anybody else to disrupt this hierarchy of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said now in your answer that you established areas of responsibility of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate these zones on the map that you already marked for us, the areas of responsibility of battalions?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence would like to present Mr. Hadzic the map so that he could indicate the battalion area of -- battalion area of responsibility. This is a document signed by Mr. Hadzic on the 29th of October 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is document P3732.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am speaking about the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion, that is what I am pointing out now. I repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you are now indicating the line which you drew as the demarcation line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But I am asking you about the battalion area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely the area of responsibility of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, the military formation of a battalion, do you know what the depth -- what the area of responsibility in depth of the battalion is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not study the military strategy in Dobrinja. Our philosophy was the defence at any price and that is the only area of responsibility. If this first line falls, if this front line falls, everything else falls as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, now you are saying if the front line falls that everything else falls. Can I can conclude from that that you had a second line behind this front line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, Ms. Pilipovic, the witness pointed at the red line pre-marked on P3732 by him. The red line which is most at the eastern side of the map, including a red line drawn to where it reads "Dobrinja." Not in italics. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, for the record, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Hadzic in indicating this line stated that this was the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where the command post of the 1st Battalion was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marked with the number five.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what the areas of responsibility of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Battalions were? And I am talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The zone, the area of responsibility, I am indicating that right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, are you telling us that this line that you are indicating as the area of responsibility of the 1st and 2nd Battalions, that this was the area of responsibility throughout the entire period of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I put to you that a witness who testified before this Chamber and who was a member of the 3rd Battalion, marked for us on this map the area of responsibility as being that of the 3rd Battalion, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well the numbers changed. It really depended. It varied. When the brigade was reorganised, then the 1st Battalion became the 3rd or the 4th one. I mean, the numbers of designating the battalions changed, but the troops were the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, you have marked for us the command post of the 3rd Battalion, as you say, with number "3."

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3, no, number 6 was the command post of the 3rd Battalion, and the area of the responsibility of the 3rd Battalion, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that these posts were permanent ones, the command posts of the battalions which were part of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that this witness who was a member of the 3rd Battalion and who testified before the Chamber on the 16th of April, 2002, on page 7294 of the transcript, marked the command post of the 3rd Battalion at the corner of Emile Zola Street, which is now called Branilaca Dobrinje?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what street it is, I don't know about that, but the battalion command posts, ever since the formation of the brigade did not change location. It is the numbers of the battalions that changed. But the locations themselves of the command posts remained the same until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the 3rd Battalion did not have its command post?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the Emile Zola Street?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that the 3rd Battalion command post was located in Dobrinja V, at the spot that I marked with number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that the command post of the 3rd Battalion was not located in the vicinity of Emile Zola Street?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and tell me where the street is?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the word "Dobrinja" written on the map? Behind or above this red dot?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Do you mean here?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hadzic, I told you where have examined a witness who was a member of the 3rd Battalion and who on page 7294 on the 16th of April 2002 indicated for us on the map the command post of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no command post here. Never. It's just that in this street here, there was a building which housed the command of the Dobrinja HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The Dobrinja HVO, you say. Are you referring to a battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To an HVO company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What battalion did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the battalion that we have been discussing, that is the 1st one, in the area of the responsibility of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are showing us this street now on the map. Is this street now called Branilaca Dobrinje?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The command post of the HVO company, in which building was the located?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am indicating this location on the map. This location used to be a shop of the Poljo Oprema company and this is what I am indicating now on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So your testimony is that the HVO company was located in the former shop of the Poljo Oprema company?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us that building.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was again an eight-storey building with several entrances.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us then that it was a residential building in Dobrinja, that people lived there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that the HVO had their command post, company command post which belonged to the 1st Battalion. Where did the 2nd, the 3rd and the 4th Battalion have their command post?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In their respective areas of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "in their respective areas of responsibility," what exactly do you mean? I mean, can you tell us if the soldiers of these companies, battalions, took their food there? I mean, where exactly did they take their meals? I am referring to the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, it was very difficult. We had a central kitchen from which we distributed food to the troops in cans. Later on, battalions organised their own canteens where they prepared food and from where they distributed food to their men at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of this area of Dobrinja and the areas of responsibility of the 1st and the 2nd Battalion, I should like to know where the kitchen was for the members of these battalions? Was there a kitchen belonging to this battalion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the food was taken to the troops at the front line, at the positions that they held, at the buildings that they held.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of which, what kind of buildings were they?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were partly destroyed and burnt down buildings whose residents had been evicted long time ago. They were situated at the front line. There were no civilians there, only soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the distance between these buildings, that is, the buildings where the soldiers were and the first buildings which were behind?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see everything on this diagram. This building, for instance, was completely empty. The next one, across the street, well, if the building was not completely destroyed, people still lived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but can you tell us what the distance between the two was, since you were a local resident?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10 or 15 metres. I mean, the width of a street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzic. Yesterday, you told us about atomic shelters. How many such shelters were they?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three such shelters which were independent, so to speak. And a number of other shelters which were located in the basements of various buildings especially in settlements A and B. Special nuclear shelters were built in Dobrinja V.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence would like the witness to mark with a black felt-tip pen, the locations of these shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I recommend that we use a thinner finer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we have a thinner black marker, we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Dobrinja V there was one atomic shelter here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please circle the location and mark it with number "1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have already a lot of numbers on it. So perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, perhaps we could use Roman numerals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it is now already done. It is "1" in a circle. So, if we perhaps do all atomic shelters numbers in circles.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, would you please mark other atomic shelters and circle them.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to mark those that were located in various buildings?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were seven in total, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, during the conflict, who used these atomic shelters?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one in Dobrinja V, that is no one used the atomic shelter in Dobrinja V.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that area for us, please? What about the others, two, three, and four?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number two was an out-patient clinic which provided medical assistance to the local residents. It was the Civilian Protection that used these premises for initial treatment of the victims of the shelling and the distribution of the humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about number three?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as number two. It was the civilian protection organisation that used it for storing food. Religious facility was also located there, and the youth club.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you told us about atomic shelter number three now and you have marked it on the map. But can you also indicate the location of the playground? Is it indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not indicated on the map, but the children played on the parking lot here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the spot with an "X."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the record, the Defence would like to point out that the plateau marked with an "X" was the one where this football match was played, whereas the atomic shelter marked with number three was nearby, parallel to the playground marked with an "X."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, that is comment. It is marked on the map. We all have the maps. We can see whether it is far away or nearby. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, atomic shelter number four?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that one, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very seldom used at the beginning as a shelter from the shelling. It used to be -- it was used for the humanitarian aid, but at one point in time it became flooded. So it was no longer used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Number five?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was used by the local residents when the warning signal was given. In cases of shelling, for instance, they would go down to the basement to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, members of the brigade under your command, did they ever use atomic shelters?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No never.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, if I tell you that we heard a witness here before this Chamber, a witness who participated in this football match, on page 6.643 of the transcript, the witness who was heard on the 4th of April, 1992, I am referring to Mr. Ismet Fazlic. Questioned by the Defence on page 6643 as to his knowledge about the existence of any barracks in Dobrinja where members of the local brigade were quartered, he replied on 6.644, lines two to six, that there were no barracks in Dobrinja, only atomic shelters. There were four atomic shelters. In Dobrinja III-A and B, because those were new buildings, there were atomic shelters which could accommodate up to 3.000 people, and it was in those atomic shelters that the headquarters of the army were located. Mr. Hadzic, can you tell us what the truth is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, this is not true. I should know where my soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you marked for us the line of the 1st Battalion on this map. Mr. Ismet Fazlic on page 6672 lines, 2 to 4, stated the following: "I am only familiar with the 1st Battalion. It was a shelter, an atomic shelter, located at the square called Djeca Dobrinja."

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I state authoritatively, that this is not true. Perhaps soldiers went into those shelters by mistake or when they were off-duty, where there was perhaps a club or something like that. But there were no soldiers there. They didn't sleep there, they didn't spend time there or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you are telling us that Mr. Ismet Fazlic who was heard here is not speaking the truth --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If my learned friend could give us a reference to the part she quoted and then please proceed. A page reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand what Ms. Pilipovic was referring to page 6672, is that correct? And then lines two to four. My problem is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do not see the words you just mentioned, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the interpreters do not have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6671, lines 24, and 25. Does he know where the command posts are of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Battalions of the 5th Motorised Brigade and the answers is on page 6672, lines two to four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read on page 6672 lines two to four, "abbreviation CZ" and Mr. Piletta-Zanin, interpretation, "yes, Mr. President, abbreviation CZ stands for..." That is what I read.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe counsel is referring to the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English version says something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: French, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you said 6672 and I think that Ms. Pilipovic said 6671. But I don't know whether you said 66 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic said 6671 for the question and 6672 for the answer. That is, at least, how it is translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes Your Honour. 6671, lines, and 25. Whether the witness knows whether the command posts of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Battalions of the 5th Motorised Brigade are and the answer is on page 6672.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on the lines indicated by you Ms. Pilipovic, it is unfortunately for everyone, it is myself who is speaking, so that could not be the question I take it. Could you perhaps try to clarify on the -- perhaps that the pages have changed since then. But, perhaps, during the break, try to find the location. Perhaps by using "search" functions or to use specific words that we could use on the same day to find the location. Perhaps Ms. Pilipovic, it would be time for a break anyhow. We will adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Until 10 minutes to 6.00. I should say five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any specific reason why the Prosecution has not yet arrived? No. I am not asking the Defence for an explanation. Perhaps someone else would know. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the break, I checked the transcript before the end of the break and it is 6669, so it is the transcript of the 4th of April, 2002. The question is: Does he know where the command posts of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th battalions are and the response is on page 6670, lines two to five. "I don't know. I only know about the 1st Battalion, that was on the atomic shelter on the square known as Djeca Dobrinja. I don't know about the others. This was a military secret."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, is it true that the command post of the 1st Battalion was in the nuclear shelter?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, so you are saying that Mr. Ismet Fazlic is not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, the Defence would like to show you document D159.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 160.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, do you have a document before you from the 1st of November 1992, the 5th Mountain Brigade of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the second page, is it your signature, your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not my signature. It is my name and my surname, but it is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature? Who signed for you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my deputy. Bicej.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, according to this document which is in the form of an order, does it start with the words: "Based on the order of the command of the 1st Corps of the 22nd of October 1992 and because of forthcoming combat activities in order to increase combat readiness of the 5th Dobrinja Mountain Brigade I order: One, immediately start with the formation of the reconnaissance sabotage platoon for the 5th Mountain Brigade Dobrinja." Is that what the states?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Under item two, does it state the number, "the strength of 25 to 30 men must be subject of priority and they should be armed with a full combat set of equipment." And under three it says "the platoon will be stationed in the facilities of Bosna Folklor where they will be accommodated in a barracks and the meals would be organised in the kitchen of the brigade command." Mr. Hadzic, is it true what the states here in this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate to us on the map where the premise where the reconnaissance sabotage platoon was located? The Bosna Folklor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Mr. Hadzic is marking the line or indicating the line vertically below the numbers two and three where the company -- where the premises of Bosna Folklor were, where this platoon was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the street, Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the Oktobarske Revolucije Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, this is a bit confusing because below two and three is upwards from the original position of this map. So, I would say that orienting ourselves on the ERN number in red on the map, it is the building up to the right, almost vertically to the numbers two and three.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, perhaps Mr. Hadzic can circle this building and mark it with the letter "b" for Bosna Folklor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, based on this order, would you agree with me that you were obliged to carry out the orders of your superior command, the command of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hadzic, you told us during the examination-in-chief yesterday that you received only a couple of mortars in 1993. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that at the end of 1993, we received one mortar of 87-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What other heavy weapons did the 5th Motorised Brigade have? I am thinking about heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We practically didn't have any in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before the next question is asked I just wonder if there could be a clarification of the answer to the previous question. I have here "87-millimetre mortar." If perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it is a mistake in the transcript. I said 82.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received a mortar of a calibre 81-millimetres at the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of 1993. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you about single or plural. If we look at the testimony of yesterday, I see we received an 81-millimetre mortar and that is at the end of 1993. And then later on we are talking about the plural of 60-millimetre mortars, mortars with an "s." Because now we are dealing with the plural for the 81-millimetre which is different from what the testimony was. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, could you please tell us, regarding 1993, which battalion received this mortar?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mortar didn't belong to any battalion. The staff units, units had them -- had it, but actually it was used in order to train the men.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that besides that one mortar that you received at the end of 1993, and except for the weapons that you already mentioned, the guns, the rifles, you didn't have any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the course of 1992, we had some anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "anti-armour equipment" can you be a little more specific?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we had two hand-held mortars, one recoil-less cannon and one Osa.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show Mr. Hadzic a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is 161. I had heard "166."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, is this a document of the command of the 5th Motorised Brigade of the 13th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document that you signed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document in the form of an order that you issued?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Underneath the word "I order" does it say "while requesting artillery firing support from the motorised battalion exclusively used the map with the chief of artillery with marked targets when you received for usage."

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who was the chief of artillery in the command of the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the artillery of the 5th Motorised Brigade was deployed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you we didn't have any artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you send this order to, the order for artillery support?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the command of the 1st Corps, which had its mortar batteries nearby and which were used as part of the combat activities in order to protect the area of responsibility of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the corps command had positions nearby, could you indicate on the map where these positions were?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot indicate them exactly, but they were on the other side of Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "on the other side of Mojmilo," could you indicate on the map where the positions of the BH Army were on Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the edge of the Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But we have a map, sir, so if you would kindly indicate that on the map where you marked, where the positions of the 1st Corps artillery were.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact location of those positions, but I know that they were on the other side of Mojmilo hill. Mojmilo hill is here, so it was these locations somewhere below the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, Mr. Hadzic, could you please point those positions again? Could you draw a black line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, I cannot mark them exactly with a line, because I don't know exactly where they were. These positions were behind Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you accept if I were to tell you that according to you, these positions were between the words Mojmilo or Novi Grad or even more south, to the south, in relation to these words?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really tell on this map. I can't tell exactly, but they were somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that these positions were on the other side of Mojmilo, they were facing which part of the city?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said "the other side of Mojmilo." So are you saying that it was on the side of Mojmilo which faced Dobrinja and was your battalion on that side?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "our battalion"?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The 5th Motorised. Who held the positions that looked on Dobrinja, on Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not held by our brigade, this was held by the next brigade, the 101st.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that the positions of the 101st Motorised Brigade were in the area of Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show Mr. Hadzic another document, number 162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May the usher assist you. Ms. Pilipovic, may I indicates that there are 25 minutes left. Do I see that some of the documents have been marked by a marker in colour and others not?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Might even have missed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document for my use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that page 68, line 14 is a question and line 16 is the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, is this a document from the 2nd of the October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of that document, do we have the signature of Zajko Vatrenjak?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the commander -- assistant commander for intelligence duties of the 2nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the deputy --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down and make a pause between question and answer, because we are not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, you are speaking the same language as Ms. Pilipovic does, and the interpreters have some difficulties in following you, if you make no pause between question and answer. So may I invite you to make just a small pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, does it state in this document on page 3 of the document, paragraph 2, "our first line is positioned"? Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: "On the direction Mojmilo hill, Serdarevic house, Partizanska Olimpijade Street, Avde Cuka Street, Salvadora Allende Street, forest behind garage in Dobrinja IV, school Dusan Pajic-Dasic." Is this true that the line was there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which battalion held this line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does it say that the first line is well fortified and has machine-gun nests and bunkers?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us these machine-gun nests, where were they located, in which buildings?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around the line of separation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many of these nests were there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not many.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not many, what do you mean? Can you tell us approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three to four.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do we read then the line is connected with fortifications which are safe for quick transfer of personnel to the first line?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I suggest the following disposition of our forces in case of enemies attack. Anti-armour weapons should be deployed in the following way: In the trench nearby Serdarevic house, two anti-armour weapons. It says here "anti-armour", what kind of weapons were they?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what he said? We didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer, Mr. Hadzic, since the interpreters could not hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is merely a suggestion regarding the deployment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Hadzic, on page one of this document, do we read: "Intelligence report on the deployment and strength of enemy forces."

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vatrenjak, is he hereby reporting on the whereabouts of the lines in question and is he saying that the troops of the 5th Motorised Brigade should be deployed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then read: "Two anti-armour weapons, one anti-armour weapon in Partizanska Olimpijade Street." Can we read this in this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also read that one anti-armour weapon should be deployed in Salvador Allende Street?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And further down can we read that the three anti-armour weapons should be deployed in Dusan Dasic school?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well yes, that is what he writes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us in 1992, you had two hand-held launchers, one cannon and one Osa, can you tell where this gun was positioned?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was positioned along this axis, together with this Osa that we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about these two handheld launchers.

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion had one and the 3rd Battalion had the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us, therefore, Mr. Hadzic, apart from the weapons that I just indicated to you, the 5th Motorised Brigade did not have any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from these, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, what weapons were used to -- what weapons were used by your battalion which was deployed facing Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry weapons, and they had also one hand-held launcher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it changed location according to the need, but we only had very few shells for this launcher. The same went for the recoil-less gun that we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, so far we have spoken about the so-called heavy weapons. Can you now tell us whether there were any snipers in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the beginning of the war, we didn't have means or people for that. With further reorganisation of the units, we had the position which we called "marksman." Those were the people who were deployed at the front line of the defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were no snipers in the 5th Motorised Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Azem Basic. Does the name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never heard of that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I put to you that he was one of the snipers that were active in Dobrinja under your control, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I don't know a person by that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the positions near the school in Dobrinja, that is the school that we identified and in respect of which you said that the positions of the 1st Battalion were located, from these positions, were any snipers active towards Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not located at the school. We were located in the trenches around the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But who was positioned in the school building?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one. It was in such a state that it was impossible to have anyone positioned there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, on the 30th of May and the 3rd of June of this year, a member of the United Nations was heard by this Chamber. His name is Roy Thomas, he had previously given a statement to the OTP investigators on the 15th of April, 1998. In that statement, on page eight of the Serb version of the statement, paragraph four, he declared the following: "I managed to enter one of these locations, the school in Dobrinja, from where the BH Army was able to cover the road to the VRS barracks in Lukavica. This was right across the street from the church in Dobrinja. When I entered the Bosnian location, I found police officers there who appeared very professional and had good equipment." Are you aware of the fact that police officers who had been trained as snipers were using the school in Dobrinja for this purpose?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How close were positions of your battalion to the school?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were four to five metres away from the school building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often did you go -- did you visit these positions?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded in 1993. I had splinters for quite a while during that period of time and moved with difficulty. I had to walk on crutches, so I very rarely ventured all the way to those positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You were wounded from December until February?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was discharged for home treatment, after which I underwent a number of surgeries.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you were asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who replaced you during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My deputy, the Deputy Commander, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Your deputy, did he inform you of the fact that there were snipers positioned in the school in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did he -- did the battalion commander notify you of this fact?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, while you were the commander, you were never made aware of the fact that there was snipers in the school in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was your cooperation with the members of UNPROFOR like? How well did you cooperate with them?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, it was excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to take care that you do not go too quickly, would you please wait until the text stops moving. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Madam Pilipovic also wait for the interpretation, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood, Ms. Pilipovic, that you would take notice of this observation as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, my question concerned your cooperation with UNPROFOR and you said that you had very good, excellent, cooperation with them. Members of UNPROFOR, did they ever confront you with the activity of the snipers located in the Dobrinja school at any of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At least not me, personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the meetings that you had with members of UNPROFOR, did you ever launch a protest with the members of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning what?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning the activity of Serb snipers, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when please, in 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of these years, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, ever since they were stationed in the area of the airport and started visiting Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did representatives of UNPROFOR ever make you aware of the fact that they had information that snipers were active from the positions held by the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No they didn't say any such thing to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you are not aware of an sniping -- snipers' nest in the school in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I showed you the witness statement of an UN military observer for Sarajevo who declared that he was the one who had uncovered this sniper, would you agree with my assertion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is possible that the gentleman in question informed the police of that fact, because the police had their area of responsibility there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So the police had their area of responsibility in that part?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate for us specifically where this area was?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the police force was located in this building here behind the school, and some were positioned in a nearby building across the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, have you now indicated for us the positions of the police as being in the same buildings that you used?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A part of this building communications one and two was held by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Under whose command was the police which was active in this zone together with you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under Mr. Vikic's command.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that in the area of responsibility of your battalion, which, that is the 1st and the 2nd Battalion, that there was also police officer which was active under the command of Mr. Vikic? I should like to know in what other parts of Dobrinja was this police force under Vikic's command active?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in these areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you know that the Prosecution asked for 20 minutes for procedural issues or quarter of an hour. Time for cross-examination still have a couple of minutes left. What --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can my colleague and I check, because we believe that the Prosecution took two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will tell you. I will ask the -- is that true? Then, my computing was not correct, and you have more time. Nevertheless, we would like to stop -- I will check it, but the Registrar confirms that yesterday, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will check whether the -- more in detail whether the Prosecution took two and a half hours. There are some -- there never is any disagreement between the Presiding Judge and the Registrar, but now there is. But we will figure that out. Could you please conclude for today in a couple of minutes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, when you said that the Military Police under the command of Vikic acted from these positions, was that the Military Police that included also Mr. Kerim Loncarevic in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the command post of the Military Police was located, the Military Police that was on the positions from where you also operated?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, that was not the Military Police. That was a special police unit, a special MUP unit, not the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was it located?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the edge of this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, can you tell us, this place that you are indicating, is that the command post of the special police and can you tell us what street that is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, that street was called the Mitsubishi Avenue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dobrinja IIB.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, this building where the special police was located, what kind of a building was that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a pretty large building with several entrances and several floors. They were deployed in the -- it was a salon before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that in the apartments in that building that the citizens of Dobrinja lived there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to stop here and we would like to complete our cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think I made a mistake. I think you still have an hour left. Mr. Hadzic, we have to deal with a few procedural issues that will take approximately a quarter of an hour. Therefore, you will be excused for the moment. May I remind you not to speak with anyone about your testimony given in this court and we hope to see you back tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00 in the same courtroom. Yes. Mr. Usher, can you please escort Mr. Hadzic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must say that I will need five minutes in order to point out some interpretation problems for all three booths. So I would kindly ask Mr. Ierace to be quite brief, because we really mustn't work longer than 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will see what we can do. Mr. Ierace, you asked and could you please be brief, since Mr. Piletta-Zanin needs a bit more time than usual for the translation issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Mr. President. The issue that I seek to raise relates to the information on the sniping and shelling maps that were before the Trial Chamber earlier this week. Mr. President, in particular, the evidence as to the plotting of the sites where the victims to the various scheduled incidents were at the time of the impact by the bullet or shell; and secondly, the indications on those maps as to the source of fire. Mr. President, the evidence before the Trial Chamber at the moment in relation to those two classes of information, essentially comes down to eyewitness evidence in the form of direct evidence from the witness box, as well as through the various videos and photographs that have been tendered. And secondly, a statement by Zoran Lesic which is an exhibit before the Trial Chamber being P3653. I have in mind the following procedure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, is that the statement you tendered and which I found on my desk and all the other members of the Chamber as well today, the 92 bis statement or --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, that was the statement tendered through him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, when he testified, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In February. The evidence more particularly contained in that statement, to the extent it is a reproduction of GPS positions on the videotapes, is some form of evidence of those positions. Mr. President, the process that I have in mind in order to hopefully render the various sites plotted on the map as admissible is as follows: To call Zoran Lesic to give evidence to the effect that he has consulted the maps which have been tendered, in particular, the sites indicated by the red dots, that is, the sites where the victims were shot. You will recall that Mr. Lesic has effectively given evidence that he was present on each of the occasions that surviving victims and eyewitnesses were videoed, and, therefore, he is in a position to confirm the sites on the maps. You may also recall that he gave evidence that he lived in Sarajevo and is familiar with the city and that, in my respectful submission could be done properly in a matter of minutes. I would submit that it is not necessary for this witness to have blank maps and drawing on his memory and knowledge to indicate on those blank maps where those sites were. Rather, I would respectfully submit that it would be entirely acceptable for him in these circumstances to simply confirm that the indicated positions on the maps of where the victims were is, in fact, correct. I make that submission against the background that it has not been suggested to any witness that they were shot in a different location to which that appears on the video. The videos themselves and the electronic photographs are, of course, another way in which the evidence already tendered establishes those sites, but, of course, that would require the Trial Chamber to go to Sarajevo and locate the sites in that fashion. So, Mr. President, that is the first proposal that I make. As to when that could happen, it so happens that because we have now finished the evidence of Ewa Tabeau, that we have a light day on Monday. The latest information we have provided to the Defence and copied to the Trial Chamber has only one witness set down for Monday, the 29th of July, that's Faris Gavran Kapetanovic, choose evidence is of course limited in the decision to a total of less than one hour. Mr. President, there is a second issue. It transpires that the GPS readings in the statement of Zoran Lesic are incorrect. The primary explanation for that is the handheld GPS machine that was used to take Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. those readings had not been calibrated in the required manner. It seems that when one takes GPS readings, one must first place into the machine information which pertains to the particular part of the earth surface from which readings are sought. That information is contained on standard maps. I propose to, also on Monday, recall Richard Philipps to give short evidence to that effect and also to the effect that he has made the appropriate calibration modification to the figures provided in the statement of Zoran Lesic, that is, Exhibit P3653. And in all but, I think, two cases, one then has the correct GPS reading. One might wonder what the significance is of having correct GPS readings at this stage. The relevance is should there be a certain exercise engaged in, I don't go into it any further, that material could be of assistance. He will also given an explanation, as will Zoran Lesic, as to some other corrections which have to be made to the figures in the statement. Briefly, some of the figures do not accurately reproduce the GPS readings which are on the video, a minor matter. So, Mr. President, that is the issue which I wish to alert you to. Essentially I seek leave to recall Zoran Lesic and Richard Philipps. I note that a 92 bis motion was filed. I don't go into that in any further detail, except to say that the judgment of the Trial Chamber in relation to the motion may be relevant to the decision to recall him. In other words it may be convenient for a second reason that he is recalled. Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, there is one other matter. Yesterday, you said to me that for the reasons that one of the 92 bis statements is not to be tendered, we may not want to recall that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least that was the unsaid underlying idea of inform the Prosecution on the reason why the 92 bis statement was -- would not be admitted in view of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes Mr. President. The motion which accompanied the 92 bis statement did indeed refer to 15 certificates, however, there are a number of other certificates which we would wish to tender through that witness and which are apparent in the motion. The relevance of those certificates is that it will assist the Trial Chamber with the ages and the sex of the number of victims of shelling incidents in particular, shelling incident number one, which may indeed be particularly relevant at a later point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We just indicated this yesterday in order to inform you about the reasons why the Chamber decided not to admit the statement of the witness Arifagic, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, if you have got other reasons. On the other hand, I must say and I am quite sure that the other Judges in this Chamber have heard -- the Chamber have heard very frequently over the last 10 minutes the words"not accurate, not accurately" it states 15 documents, but it might be different. Especially at the end of the case where it makes it all quite complicated, the matters we are confronted with at this moment, and of course, I include the whole Kovacs issue in that as well. But I do understand what -- that you say that the Prosecution might call the witness Arifagic anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, those additional documents are, in fact, included in the motion filed on the 6th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have to check. We try to trace all the documents and on the basis of that we -- I informed you yesterday about the reason why the -- why the Chamber decided not to admit the 92 bis statement. We will reconsider it tomorrow and work further on it and tell you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Ms. Pilipovic, any quick response?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No response?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Impossible today. But we will have some tomorrow morning with your permission. They took 10 minutes to explain to us their futuristic view of the proceedings in the future. I think I need four minutes for my own problems and then tomorrow morning, with your permission we will explain what our position is in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is, that we do not sit tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the other hand, we might be willing to consider at least part of the questions tomorrow morning. So if you could -- if the interpreters would grant us five minutes extra, at least give us some short response -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- An idea --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With pleasure. I suggest the following, Mr. President: We will give you a brief answer and that a written answer will follow in greater detail this evening so that you can work on it tomorrow morning. I think the problem is as follows: This is purely -- this is pure science fiction. We have been told today that one can count on that, that we can rely on it, but everything is false. Then if everything is false everything should be rejected in its entirety. As regards the reappearance of witness Lesic there was plenty opportunity to ask technical questions of this witness, and there was also ample opportunity to ask specific questions about specific incidents and specific events. Why are we proceeding now this manner, in violation of the Rules? If we have to bring back the witness, then the Rules will be violated. It is quite evident. If we do this now, as you have indicated at the end of the proceedings, it will be contradictory to the interest of the Defence, not only contradictory to the interest but to the rights of the Defence. If GPS were a beautiful, reliable system, then how everything can be wrong. I think I have discussed it -- addressed the issue enough and the Defence cannot accept the proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say that and the Chamber is very grateful to the Defence that they with willing to put in more detail their thoughts on paper so that we can read it tomorrow morning. That really assists us greatly and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... than those who are assisting us. We will consider the matters and we will consider how important this whole GPS is for the Chamber at this very moment. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you needed a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be very quick. So each time I will give the page and the line number. And then I will state what I think. So page 12, line 9, on several occasions it was 92, then 13, 15 we said one booth. So from the French booth it was "hospitals" the plural. Then page 17, line -- so D25 not it is not 25, it is D21. Page 37 line 23, I heard in the Serbian text that the witness said "I couldn't say that," which is not the same as "I don't know." So there is a difference. "Overlooks" should be translated differently. On page 41, line 15, I think I heard the witness say "all ethnicities" which was not correctly interpreted as various ethnicities. 50 something page, line 10, which said that the republican police is not the same as the Military Police. Page 51, line 13, italics, it should be Dobrinja written in italics. So in the French booth, the meaning wasn't conveyed. And then page 51, 23, two witness answers are missing as well as one answer by the Defence. The witness intervened. I think he said in Serbian "buildings immediately next to" while the response of the Defence was "yes, yes" on page 74.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The English booth just ask that Mr. Piletta-Zanin slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't hear that. I heard some -- yes, would you please -- I think if you do it too quickly and you have to repeat it, that takes even more time than doing it a bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologises Page 74 for the French booth,"the road to the church" and not "to church". Page 76, line 10, I think the witness added "no, no, no" but I didn't hear the rest. I think it can by found in the transcript. Page 76, line 24, I think that the words "preko ceste" were not interpreted or the interpretation was an erroneous one, and I think that would be it for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one remark to make. First, the Chamber has considered the matter when a witness list and a list of exhibits should be presented. The Defence is required to present a provisional witness list and a provisional exhibit list immediately after the close of the Prosecution's case. That would enable at least the Prosecution to start working on it during the recess. So that would be presumably the 2nd of August, by the end of the day. And then tomorrow morning, I would like to start in closed session to hear the answer on the question which is still a confidential issue, a question that has been put to the Defence last Friday and on which the Chamber would like to have an answer. Is it clear enough for you? Otherwise we should have -- there was a question about whether under certain special circumstances the position of the Defence would remain the same or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My colleague is nodding and I am nodding too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we will tomorrow perhaps start in closed session just for one or two minutes. We will adjourn until tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.07 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
